texts.facts: Heard. 3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 10.10.2001, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased four sealed packets of tea dust from the first accused. The second accused was the distributor of the said item. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P22 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item and was, therefore adulterated. It was further reported in Ext.P22 report that the sample contained added synthetic colours, namely, tartrazine, sunset yellow food colour and carmoisine and therefore, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P36 series were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined and Ext.D1 was marked on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 6. When this matter has been taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that in view of the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176], there is no need to remand the matter to adduce evidence for availing the benefit under Section 19(2) of the P.F.A. Act and in the said circumstances, the learned counsel has pleaded for setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court remanding the case to the trial court.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 6. When this matter has been taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that in view of the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176], there is no need to remand the matter to adduce evidence for availing the benefit under Section 19(2) of the P.F.A. Act and in the said circumstances, the learned counsel has pleaded for setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court remanding the case to the trial court.
